review_notes: I read the whole file and the three `*_generator_zero` proofs in full. I compared them with Mathlib's `hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_of_tendsto_deriv`. I also looked at the other repeated-looking pieces: the `realHeatList_*` induction proofs, the `HasDerivAt`/`HasDerivWithinAt` product rules in `EulerStrongOperatorDerivative`, and the `hD`/`hDD` jet-word coordinate proofs. Those are short, or differ in substance, so I did not report them. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemma and rewrites are untested. I expect `Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Extend` to be available through the existing imports, because the current proofs already use the Mathlib lemma it contains.

findings.problem: Three theorems repeat the same argument for extending a positive-time derivative formula to a right derivative at 0. Each one (1) builds a `Tendsto` of the half-generator along `𝓝[>] 0` from continuity of `s ↦ (1/2) • heat s X` and the value at time 0, (2) applies `hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_of_tendsto_deriv (s := Set.Ioi 0)` with differentiability taken from the positive-time `HasDerivAt`, (3) rewrites the limit with `hlim.congr'`, and (4) uses `(…generator_pos …).deriv.symm`. Only the family, its continuity lemma and its time-zero lemma differ. The proof is about 15 lines, copied three times at 178–193, 429–448 and 531–551. The cylinder copy has slightly different bookkeeping, so the copies can drift apart.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one general lemma before `realLineHeat_generator_zero`, for example in a small namespace such as `EulerGaussianCylinderHeat`:

`theorem hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_zero_of_pos {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {φ ψ : ℝ → E} (hφ : Continuous φ) (hψ : Continuous ψ) (hd : ∀ t, 0 < t → HasDerivAt φ (ψ t) t) : HasDerivWithinAt φ (ψ 0) (Set.Ici 0) 0`

Proof sketch: apply `hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_of_tendsto_deriv (s := Set.Ioi 0)`. Differentiability on `Ioi 0` is `fun t ht => (hd t ht).differentiableAt.differentiableWithinAt`. Continuity is `hφ.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt`, and `hs` is `self_mem_nhdsWithin`. For the limit, take `(hψ.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt (s := Set.Ioi 0)).tendsto`, then `.congr'` with `filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with t ht; exact (hd t ht).deriv.symm`.

Rewritten uses:
- Line: take `φ = fun s => realLineHeat period a s f`, `ψ = fun s => (1/2:ℝ) • realLineHeat period a s h`. The hypotheses are `realLineHeat_continuous period a f`, `(realLineHeat_continuous period a h).const_smul _` and `realLineHeat_generator_pos period a f g h hD hDD`. Then `simpa only [realLineHeat_zero] using` the lemma.
- List: take `φ = fun s => realHeatList period (indices.map direction) s f`, `ψ = fun s => (1/2:ℝ) • realHeatList period (indices.map direction) s ((indices.map ddf).sum)`. Use `realHeatList_continuous` and `realHeatList_generator_pos period indices direction f df ddf hD hDD`. Finish with `simpa only [realHeatList_zero_time]`.
- Cylinder: take `φ = fun s => realCylinderHeat period s f`, `ψ = fun s => (1/2:ℝ) • realCylinderHeat period s (jetLaplacian period J)`. Continuity comes from `(cylinderHeat_continuous period _).comp continuous_real_toNNReal`, and the derivative from `realCylinderHeat_generator_pos period J`. Finish with `simpa only [realCylinderHeat, Real.toNNReal_zero, cylinderHeat_zero]`.

These rewrites apply under the current hypotheses and imports, since the positive-time derivative theorems are already stated as `HasDerivAt … t` for all `0 < t`.
findings.benefit: Each `_generator_zero` theorem shrinks to a few lines: continuity facts, the positive-time generator, and a time-zero simplification. The one-sided-derivative extension argument gets a single named statement, so a reader sees what is specific to each semigroup. Future changes to the limit argument are made once, not three times, and further heat families can reuse the lemma.
